overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: no quorum of the Council deliberated outside a meeting about the Town Manager, so the complaint was closed.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged Council members held discussions outside meetings and acted with enough votes to control outcomes, and that members left a meeting to defeat quorum.
allegations.key_passage: it does not violate the Open Meeting Law, because a quorum of the Council is not engaging in a deliberation as defmed by G.L. c. 30A, §18.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a former councilor told the Town Manager he had six votes to remove him and sought a seventh councilor's commitment, a serial deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: it does not appear that Mr. Crocker spoke with six or more Council members outside of a meeting regarding the Town Manager's employment.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
